etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English joinen, joynen, joignen, from Old French joindre, juindre, jungre, from Latin iungō (“join, yoke”, verb), from Proto-Indo-European *yewg- (“to join, unite”). Cognate with Old English iucian, iugian, ġeocian, ġyċċan (“to join; yoke”). More at yoke.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To connect or combine into one; to put together.
(intransitive) To enter into association or alliance, to unite in a common purpose.
